title: A nontrivial finite p-group has a normal subgroup of index p
statement: Let $p$ be a prime natural number and let $P$ be a group with finite underlying set [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set] and $|P|=p^a$ for an integer $a\geq1$. Then there is a subgroup $H\subseteq P$ such that $gHg^{-1}=H$ for every $g\in P$ and $[P:H]=p$. Here $|P|$ denotes the number of elements, and $[P:H]$ the number of left cosets of $H$ in $P$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, third proof paragraph: the group-theoretic refinement implicit in the use of solvability of inertia after Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia. The asserted group-theoretic tool is agent-supplied; its independent induction proof is recorded in the delivery report.

proof.text: Write $a=b+1$ with $b\geq0$. Since $|P|=p^{b+1}=p^b p$, the prime power $p^b$ divides $|P|$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-subgroup-prime-power-order] to the finite group $P$, the given prime $p$, and $n=b$. Obtain a subgroup $H\subseteq P$ with $|H|=p^b$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, third proof paragraph (finite normal-extension filtration), after Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia; agent-supplied group-theoretic argument, using the cited Mathlib tools.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-surjective-subgroup-image-index] with both groups equal to $P$, the identity surjection, and $L=H$, so that its image $J$ is $H$. Its order-index formula gives $|H|[P:H]=|P|$. Substitution yields $p^b[P:H]=p^{b+1}=p^b p$. Since $p$ is prime, $p\geq2$ and $p^b>0$; cancellation in the natural numbers gives $[P:H]=p$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, third proof paragraph (finite normal-extension filtration), after Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia; agent-supplied group-theoretic argument, using the cited Mathlib tools.

proof.text: The least prime divisor of $|P|=p^{b+1}$ is $p$. Indeed $p$ divides this integer. Any prime $q$ dividing it must equal $p$: induction on the exponent and the elementary prime-divides-product rule show that $q\mid p^{b+1}$ implies $q\mid p$, and a prime divisor of the prime $p$ is $p$. The exponent is positive, so $|P|\geq p>1$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, third proof paragraph (finite normal-extension filtration), after Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia; agent-supplied group-theoretic argument, using the cited Mathlib tools.

proof.text: The subgroup $H$ from step 1 has index $p$ by step 2, and $p$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|P|>1$ by step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-least-prime-index-normal] to $G=P$ and this $H$. It gives $gHg^{-1}=H$ for every $g\in P$, while the already computed index is $p$. These are the two required properties of the same subgroup.
